questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the y-Intercepts of an Ellipse
questions.problem: Determine the points where the ellipse $3{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=24$ intercepts the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the $y$-intercept, we need to substitute $x=0$ in the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $y.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-24 & =0 \\ 3\cdot {0}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-24 & =0 \\ 4{y}^{2}-24 & =0 \\ 4{y}^{2} & =24 \\ {y}^{2} & =6 \\ y & =\pm \sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $y$-axis at the points $(0,-\sqrt{6})$ and $(0,\sqrt{6}).$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the x-Intercepts of an Ellipse By Completing the Square
questions.problem: Calculate the points where the ellipse $2{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}-20x+6y+47=0$ intercepts the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the $x$-intercepts, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $x.$ We do this and solve the resulting equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}-20x+6y+47 & =0 \\ 2{x}^{2}+3(0)^{2}-20x+6(0)+47 & =0 \\ 2{x}^{2}-20x+47 & =0 \\ 2[{x}^{2}-10x]+47 & =0 \\ 2[(x-5)^{2}-25]+47 & =0 \\ 2(x-5)^{2}-50+47 & =0 \\ 2(x-5)^{2} & =3 \\ (x-5)^{2} & =\frac{3}{2} \\ x-5 & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \\ x & =5\pm \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $x$-axis at $(5-\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}},0)$ and $(5+\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}},0).$

questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the $y$-intercept, we need to substitute $x=0$ in the equation of the ellipse and try to solve the resulting equation for $y.$ We do this and solve the resulting equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-12x+8y+4 & =0 \\ 3(0)^{2}+4{y}^{2}-12(0)+8y+4 & =0 \\ 4{y}^{2}+8y+4 & =0 \\ 4\,[{y}^{2}+2y]+4 & =0 \\ 4[(y+1)^{2}-1]+4 & =0 \\ 4(y+1)^{2}-4+4 & =0 \\ 4(y+1)^{2} & =0 \\ (y+1)^{2} & =0 \\ y+1 & =0 \\ y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $y$-axis at the point $(0,-1).$

questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the $y$-intercept, we need to substitute $x=0$ in the equation of the ellipse and try to solve the resulting equation for $y.$ We do this and solve the resulting equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}+25{y}^{2}-40x+100y+100 & =0 \\ 4(0)^{2}+25{y}^{2}-40(0)+100y+100 & =0 \\ 25{y}^{2}+100y+100 & =0 \\ 25\,[{y}^{2}+4y+4] & =0 \\ 25\,(y+2)^{2} & =0 \\ (y+2)^{2} & =0 \\ y & =-2\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the x-Intercepts of an Ellipse By Completing the Square
questions.problem:
Calculate the point where the ellipse  $5{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-20x+16y+20=0$ intercepts the $x$-axis.

The $x$-intercept is $($
{{field-1}}
,
{{field-2}}$).$
questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the $x$-intercepts, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $x.$ We do this and solve the resulting equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-20x+16y+20 & =0 \\ 5{x}^{2}+4\cdot {0}^{2}-20x+16\cdot 0+20 & =0 \\ 5{x}^{2}-20x+20 & =0 \\ 5\,[{x}^{2}-4x]+20 & =0 \\ 5[(x-2)^{2}-4]+20 & =0 \\ 5(x-2)^{2}-20+20 & =0 \\ 5(x-2)^{2} & =0 \\ x-2 & =0 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $x$-axis at  $(2,0).$
